objective: Test whether Trainable HiGS exhibits increasing training-time advantage over conventional gsplat as scene density, resolution, and camera workload scale

hypotheses.H1: Hierarchical rendering provides increasing benefit with workload scale (PRIMARY)
hypotheses.H2: Forward hierarchy helps, but native backward dominates and prevents training scaling
hypotheses.H3: Hierarchy rebuild / dynamic-topology overhead erases the rendering advantage
hypotheses.H4: HiGS benefit is primarily visibility/culling dependent rather than workload-scale dependent
hypotheses.H5: HiGS only wins in fixed-state rendering, not real dynamic training
hypotheses.H6: Apparent gains come from unmatched semantics/protocol rather than architecture

MED_N.scene: Not available in current dataset collection
MED_N.notes: Can be synthesized by loading garden (if available) or subsampling bicycle

stage_a_correctness.result: PASS - 100 tests, gradient cosine ~1.0, quality parity within noise

protocol.notes: Frozen topology (no densify); measure fwd/bwd/total/train VRAM

stage_c_scaling_law_analysis.description: Fit descriptive models to workload-speedup relationships

stage_d_dynamic_topology_cost.reference_data: Round-10 report: pack 3.2 ms, construct 0.35 ms, amortized ~1.4 ms/step @ 20 steps with densify every 5

stage_e_full_training_validation.status: CONDITIONAL (only if stage B shows meaningful gain)

gate.condition: At least TWO dense/high-workload points with S_FB >= 1.15x AND at least one with S_FB >= 1.20x

stage_e_full_training_validation.expected_duration: 30K steps × 4 backends × 3 scenes × 2 arms = ~72 training runs

expected_outcomes.if_H1_true: LOW-N: parity/slower; MID-N: modest gain; HIGH-N: strong gain (>=1.20x)
expected_outcomes.if_H2_true: Forward parity/slower, backward parity/slower (native doesn't help vs std)
expected_outcomes.if_H3_true: Fixed-state shows gain, but dynamic topology erases it
expected_outcomes.if_H4_true: Speedup correlates with culling_ratio, not N/pixels/batch
expected_outcomes.if_H5_true: Frozen native shows gain, dynamic erases it (similar to H3)
expected_outcomes.if_H6_true: Speedup only when protocol differs (B has hidden overhead)

execution_requirements.software: Linux, CUDA 12.8/12.9, torch 2.9.1+cu128, patched gsplat with HiGS

estimated_duration.stage_b: ~2-4 hours (7 workload points × 2 backends × 20 steps × ~10 sec/step)
estimated_duration.stage_d: ~1 hour (2 scenes × 2 backends × 20 steps with densify)
estimated_duration.stage_e: ~48-72 hours (conditional, only if stage B passes gate)

checks: nvidia-smi to verify no foreign processes
